summary: Argentina grants visa-free entry of up to 90 days to citizens of the US, Canada, the UK, the EU, Australia, Japan and most of the Americas, and offers an electronic travel authorization (AVE) to some visa-required nationals who hold a valid US visa.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Argentina?
faq.answer: No. US citizens enter Argentina visa-free for tourism for up to 90 days.

faq.question: Can I extend my 90-day stay in Argentina?
faq.answer: Yes. Migraciones allows a tourist stay to be extended once for a similar period; request the extension (prórroga de permanencia) from the Dirección Nacional de Migraciones before your initial stay expires.

faq.question: Do Chinese citizens need a visa for Argentina?
faq.answer: Chinese citizens need a consular tourist visa unless they hold a valid US visa, in which case they can enter without a visa or an AVE for tourism or business, for up to 30 days. Chinese citizens no longer apply for the AVE.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccine for Iguazú Falls?
faq.answer: It is not an entry requirement for Argentina, but the Ministry of Health counts Misiones, Corrientes, Formosa and parts of Jujuy, Salta and Chaco as yellow fever risk areas and recommends vaccination at least 10 days before visiting areas with transmission.

faq.question: Should I bring cash or use cards in Argentina?
faq.answer: Canada's travel advice says foreign credit and debit cards are accepted in main cities, but ATM withdrawals on foreign cards are subject to low limits and substantial service charges may apply. You may be asked for photo ID, such as a copy of your passport, when paying by card.
